D1_oob.root_cause: PyList_Check/PyTuple_Check accept SUBCLASSES. PySequence_Size() then dispatches to an attacker-overridden __len__ whose return value does not describe the real storage. That value sized the C arrays AND bounded PySequence_Fast_GET_ITEM(), which is an out-of-bounds array read when __len__ over-reports and a SILENT CUSTODY TRUNCATION when it under-reports.

before_evidence.stage_a_asan: ASAN SEGV, process exit 134, crash inside PyObject_GetAttrString on an out-of-bounds pointer, from a 1-element list whose __len__ claimed 5
before_evidence.stage_a_plain_oob_read: error message 'stage A admission: relation[1] must expose ref' proves index 1 was read from a 1-element list
before_evidence.stage_b_oob_read: error message 'stage B admission: relation[1] must be exact SourceUniverseRelation' proves index 1 was read from a 1-element container
before_evidence.stage_a_silent_truncation: 3 relations supplied, __len__ claimed 0, result: sealed=True with n_relations=0
before_evidence.stage_b_silent_truncation: 1 relation supplied, __len__ claimed 0, result: sealed with n_relations=0 and a custody_hash

D1_oob.repair: accept ONLY PyList_CheckExact / PyTuple_CheckExact, then convert with PySequence_Fast and derive EVERY allocation and iteration bound from PySequence_Fast_GET_SIZE of the converted sequence. Applied to relations AND authority_snapshots on both A and B. The decide() request container check was tightened to exact types as well.

after_evidence.stage_a_asan: exit 1, NO AddressSanitizer report; clean typed refusal
after_evidence.stage_a_plain: TypeError: stage A admission requires an EXACT list or tuple (not a subclass) of relations
after_evidence.stage_b_plain: SourceRelationIntegrityError: stage B admission requires an EXACT list or tuple (not a subclass) of relations
after_evidence.truncation: no longer reachable; subclass containers are refused by type before any length is consulted
after_evidence.reentrant_len: a __len__ that would record being called is never invoked; test_d1_reentrant_len_subclass_is_refused_without_side_effect asserts the call list stays empty

D1_oob.tests: 12 lie variants x list/tuple on Stage A, 8 lie variants x relations/snapshots on Stage B, plus a reentrant case and a positive anti-truncation control

D2_refcount.stage_a_measurement_before: 20,000 custody_diagnostic() calls produced +19,999 tracked gc lists (one leaked Py_BuildValue 'rows' list per call)
D2_refcount.stage_a_root_cause: Py_BuildValue's 'O' format does NOT steal a reference, so the owned rows list was never released
D2_refcount.stage_a_measurement_after: 20,000 calls create 1 gc-tracked object total after warmup; sys.getallocatedblocks delta < 0.01 blocks/call

stage_b_findings.leak_1: ref_dict_copy() discarded the owned probe returned by dget(ad,'kind') - one object leaked per call
stage_b_findings.leak_2: exact_key_of() assigned dget(ref,'kind') to k2 and then never released it when the probe succeeded - one object leaked per call
stage_b_findings.leak_3: mk_decision() unconditionally Py_XDECREF'd relation_ref/authority_ref, which are BORROWED parameters, releasing a caller-owned reference (an over-DECREF, not a leak)
stage_b_findings.residual_unresolved: a residual ~15 allocated blocks per decide() call remains, localised by systematic bisection to the post-loop source-ref ORDERING block (PyList_Sort + keys/vals lists + dedupe + PyList_AsTuple). exact_key_of() and ref_dict_copy() were each exonerated by isolated bisection (0.001 and 0.024 blocks/call). NOT isolated further; carried as a named blocker.

D2_refcount.measurement_method: sys.getallocatedblocks() deltas after a 1000-5000 call warmup with gc disabled, plus gc.get_objects() id-set deltas as a cross-check. The naive len(gc.get_objects()) comparison used earlier is NOT trusted: it produced a false positive from interpreter lazy state.

D3_lifecycle.defect: a failed __init__ left the pinned trusted_semantic_hash, the pinned exception refs, the relations array and partially admitted relations in place
D3_lifecycle.repair: transactional initialisation. Every fallible step after pinning (PySequence_Fast, admit_relation, admit_snapshot, compute_custody_hash, custody hash allocation) now branches to fail_init, which calls the full release and returns -1. Nothing is left pinned and nothing is left partially sealed.

evidence.stage_b_20k_failed_inits: trusted semantic_hash, canonicalize and require_positive_authority refcounts each grow by at most 2 after 20,000 failing constructions
evidence.stage_b_2k_failed_inits: the admitted relation's refcount grows by at most 2 after 2,000 failing constructions - no partial custody accumulates

D4_module_init.defect: Stage B ignored three PyModule_AddObject return values; Stage A double-released a statically-held error reference on failure
D4_module_init.repair: every AddObject return is checked on both modules. On failure the module is discarded and only references this function still owns are released; the failing AddObject's partially-added object is never released twice.
D4_module_init.oom_injection: reliable OOM injection was not performed. This is recorded as source-justified rather than tested: the repaired paths use the standard CPython idiom of releasing only locally owned references and discarding the module, and every AddObject return is now checked. A reviewer wanting OOM injection should treat this as an explicit open item.

D5_gc_cycles.defect: both owner types held strong PyObject references with no tp_traverse/tp_clear, so any object graph referring back to the owner was uncollectable
D5_gc_cycles.repair: Py_TPFLAGS_HAVE_GC added, with tp_traverse visiting every held reference (trusted callables, pinned classes, exception refs, admitted relations, relation ref dicts, canonicalised scopes, admitted snapshots, authority ref dicts) and tp_clear releasing them all. Stage A additionally visits and clears its pinned registry object.
D5_gc_cycles.evidence: test_d5_owner_participates_in_cyclic_gc builds 500 owners each embedded in a cycle that refers back to the owner, then asserts the allocated-block growth stays bounded rather than linear.
D5_gc_cycles.no_impossible_claim: cycles were NOT declared impossible; a discriminating construction-and-refcount test was written instead, as the commission required.

preserved.stage_b_custody_hash_byte_exact: preserved - still equals the production Python owner_custody_hash
